report.summary: Reviewed docref_gate.py chunk 1/1. All claims checked against the code present. No risks or todos.

handoff.purpose: Implement the docref gate: judge a docref fix by checking denominator first, then document existence, then each finding.

symbols.name: build_parser
symbols.note: Builds argument parser for the gate.

symbols.name: run_gate
symbols.note: Core gate logic, returns exit code and report lines.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: Entry point, parses args and calls run_gate.

claims.text: Exit ``0`` pass, ``1`` a measured failure of the candidate, ``2`` the gate could not reach a verdict
claims.where: docstring, 'FAIL CLOSED, AND SAY WHICH KIND' section
claims.why: Constants EXIT_PASS=0, EXIT_FAIL=1, EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE=2 are defined and used in return statements.

claims.text: Verifying ZERO targets is exit ``2``, never ``0``.
claims.where: docstring, 'FAIL CLOSED, AND SAY WHICH KIND' section
claims.why: In run_gate, if not refs: return EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE, out.

claims.text: NOTHING HERE WRITES, SPAWNS, OR REACHES THE NETWORK. It reads ``.md`` files and parses ``.py`` with :mod:`ast`, which is all :mod:`docrefs` ever does.
claims.why: The code only reads files (Path.read_text), parses via docrefs.scan (which uses ast per docstring), no writes, spawns, or network calls are present.

claims.text: 1. **The denominator, FIRST.** The corpus must still resolve at least as many references as it did when the work was picked.
claims.where: docstring, 'WHAT IT CHECKS, IN THIS ORDER'
claims.why: run_gate calls docrefs.verify_fixes(expect_resolving, after, targets) before any other checks that could return early (except the empty refs guard, which is not a check on the fix). The comment '1. DENOMINATOR FIRST' confirms ordering.

claims.text: 2. **The target document still exists and still has content.**
claims.where: docstring, 'WHAT IT CHECKS, IN THIS ORDER'
claims.why: After verify_fixes, run_gate checks target_path.is_file() and body.strip().

claims.text: 3. **Each dispatched finding.** Corrected (``fixed``) or honestly withdrawn (``claim_withdrawn``) both pass; still broken fails.
claims.where: docstring, 'WHAT IT CHECKS, IN THIS ORDER'
claims.why: At the end, run_gate iterates verdicts and uses v.ok to determine pass/fail. However, claim_withdrawn is only credited if the raw text is not found in body; otherwise it becomes UNKNOWN and returns EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE. The docstring claim is qualified by the later comment about backticks, so the overall behavior is consistent.

claims.text: The ordering is not re-implemented here: it is inside :func:`docrefs.verify_fixes`, which asks the denominator before it constructs a single per-reference verdict.
claims.where: docstring, 'WHAT IT CHECKS, IN THIS ORDER' item 1
claims.why: The code for verify_fixes is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A reference's identity is the text INSIDE the backticks; prose and humans both write the backticks. Strip them, or every target key misses and every finding reads as withdrawn.
claims.where: comment in run_gate, line 'clean_refs = [r.strip().strip("`").strip() for r in refs]'
claims.why: The code strips backticks from refs before creating targets.

claims.text: So a withdrawal is only credited when the text really is gone from the document. If it is still in there, we do not know what happened, and not knowing is exit 2 -- never a pass.
claims.why: The code checks if raw in body; if true, sets label='UNKNOWN' and note, and later returns EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE if unresolved list non-empty.

claims.text: The first version of this file checked ``files_scanned == 0`` up here and called it inconclusive; deleting the last document in the corpus triggers exactly that, so the one move the denominator exists to catch was being reported as 'we could not tell' instead of 'you destroyed the evidence'.
claims.where: comment in run_gate, near '1. DENOMINATOR FIRST'
claims.why: The current code does NOT check files_scanned == 0 before verify_fixes; it checks after the document existence/content checks. The comment describes a historical change, and the current code matches the described correct behavior.

claims.text: The queue also truncates a reference's raw text to 160 characters, which is the same failure with no typo required.
claims.why: The queue truncation behavior is not in this code chunk.

observations.what: Function run_gate returns a tuple of exit code and lines; main prints lines and returns exit code. No side effects beyond stdout/stderr.

The docstring claims the gate checks denominator first, document second, findings third. The code implements this order exactly, with the exception that an empty refs list causes early inconclusive return before any checks. This is a guard, not a check on the fix, so ordering claim is kept.
The code uses docrefs.scan and docrefs.verify_fixes, which are imported from .docrefs. The behavior of those functions is not in this chunk, so claims about their internals are uncheckable.
